name: אֶתְבַּעַל
summary: King of the Sidonians, father of Jezebel, whom Ahab married, after which “he went and served the Baal and bowed down to him” (1Ki 16:31). A Phoenician name with בַּעַל, the god of Tyre and Sidon. Its first part is read either as אֶת “with”, “with Baal”, or as the Phoenician and Ugaritic word for “there is”, “Baal is”, as in Eshbaal; scripture does not say.

evidence.note: “He took as wife Jezebel daughter of אֶתְבַּעַל king of the Sidonians, and went and served the Baal.”
“He raised an altar for the Baal in the house of the Baal which he built in Samaria.”

evidence.locator: p. 81, ʾŠBʿL = YŠBʿL, p.n. (“Baal is alive”); “Compare Heb. ʾešbaʿal (1 Chronicles 8:33); Ug. iṯbʿl”
evidence.note: The Ugaritic name iṯbʿl, with iṯ “there is”, is the reading “Baal is” for אֶתְבַּעַל.

note: a.gn.ab has an empty root in the database; BDB lists the name under א with no root. Filed under בעל for the god's name. Whether אֶת is “with” or the Ugaritic iṯ is open.
